title: Void Ending in an Opposition to Mercury
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The opposition is the hardest figure the Moon can close on: the text grades it as extreme enmity, because the signs it joins stand opposed across all four natural qualities. It shares with the square the warnings that guard every election, and a Moon waning in light and faced by Saturn is the source's own example of a serious misfortune.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with an opposition to Mercury, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his quicksilver turn of mind. Mercury is intellect's planet: learning, dialectic, geometry, astronomy, writing, and the reading of tongues, with every craft found by subtle talent under his governance. He rules the tongue, the brain, and the sensory memory, and quicksilver among the metals. The electional doctrine guards him closely: a work founded on Mercury must not find him retrograde, burning in the Sun's beams, or under an unfortunate planet's gaze.
